payload.title: GPU Architecture Deep Dive
payload.summary: > A synthesis of multiple technical articles from the Zhihu community, covering SM microarchitecture, memory hierarchy, SIMT execution model, warp scheduling mechanisms, thread block scheduling strategies, and more.

sections.heading: 1. SM Microarchitecture Analysis
sections.gist: The SM (Streaming Multiprocessor) is the core compute unit of a GPU.

sections.heading: 2. Memory Hierarchy
sections.gist: The GPU memory hierarchy ranges from registers to HBM, with decreasing bandwidth and increasing latency:

sections.heading: 3. SIMT Execution Model
sections.gist: **Warp Composition**: 32 threads form a warp, executing in SIMT (Single Instruction, Multiple Threads) fashion—all threads execute the same instruction but operate on different data.

sections.heading: 4. Instruction Issue and Control Mechanisms
sections.gist: NVIDIA GPU SASS instructions embed hardware scheduling information, with every 3 instructions sharing a 128-bit control word.

sections.heading: 5. Thread Block Scheduling Strategy
sections.gist: Through empirical research on Pascal, Volta, and Turing architectures, the actual behavior of NVIDIA's thread block scheduler was revealed—it is not simple Round-Robin, but rather a **Largest Space Policy**:

sections.heading: 6. Memory System Evolution: From V100 to B200
sections.gist: As GPU bandwidth continues to grow, but the number of SMs grows even faster, the bandwidth per SM is actually increasing.

sections.heading: 7. GPU Optimization Hierarchy Summary
sections.gist: From bottom to top, GPU optimization spans multiple levels:

sections.heading: Related Documents
sections.gist: - NVIDIA Compute Capabilities — Detailed table of SM resource limits for each architecture - NVIDIA Architecture-Specific Optimization — …

implementation.snippet:
```
A100 GPU
├── 8 GPC (Graphics Processing Cluster)
│   ├── Each GPC contains 8 TPC (Texture Processing Cluster)
│   │   └── Each TPC contains 2 SM
│   └── Total 128 SM (actually available: 108)
├── L2 Cache: 40 MB
├── HBM2e: 80 GB, bandwidth 2039 GB/s
└── NVLink 3.0: 600 GB/s
```

```
Register
    ↓ ~1 cycle, ~19.5 TB/s (per SM)
L1 Cache / Shared Memory
    ↓ ~5 cycles, ~several TB/s
L2 Cache
    ↓ ~tens of cycles, ~4-6 TB/s
Global Memory (HBM)
    ~500 cycles, ~2-3 TB/s
```

```
bytes_in_flight = bandwidth × latency
```

```
estimated_bytes_in_flight_per_SM
    = (#loads/thread) × (#bytes/load) × (#threads/block) × (#blocks/SM)
```

```
                 ┌─────────────┐
                 │ Active Warps│ ← From schedule start to execution finish
                 │  (on SM)    │
                 └──────┬──────┘
                        │
              ┌─────────┴─────────┐
              │                   │
      ┌───────┴───────┐   ┌──────┴──────┐
      │ Eligible Warps│   │Stalled Warps│
      │ (ready to run)│   │ (waiting)   │
      └───────┬───────┘   └─────────────┘
              │
      ┌───────┴───────┐
      │ Selected Warps│ ← Each scheduler selects 1
      │  (executing)  │
      └───────────────┘
```

```cpp
if (threadIdx.x < 16) {
    // Branch A: first 16 threads
    path_A();
} else {
    // Branch B: last 16 threads
    path_B();
}
```

```
                    ┌── Barrier 0 ──┐
LDG R2, [R4]  ──►  │  counter: 1   │  ← load starts, counter +1
    ...             │               │
    ...             │  counter: 0   │  ← load completes, counter -1
IADD R5, R2, R3 ◄──┘               │  ← wait for barrier 0 to zero
```
